findings.title: Feature-gated table visualization discards the query result
findings.body: When `use-table-widget-visualization` is enabled, the dashboard table branch renders `TableWidgetVisualization` with `columns={[]}` and an empty `tableData` object instead of passing `fields`, `result.data`, and `result.meta`. Consequently every enabled dashboard table is blank regardless of the query response, whereas the fallback branch renders the actual result.

findings.title: Attribute-key query cache is shared across organizations
findings.body: The new React Query key contains only `queryOptions`, which does not include the organization slug. Since the fetch function closes over the current organization but the cache key remains identical after switching organizations with the same time range/projects/type, React Query can serve attribute keys fetched for the previous organization and may not refetch them. Include the organization slug (or endpoint path) in the query key.

findings.title: Mutually exclusive report fields are accepted when one is zero
findings.body: The age/timestamp exclusivity checks use truthiness of `self.initial_data`. A report containing both `timestamp: 0` and `age: 0` (or either field at zero alongside the other) bypasses the corresponding validation even though both fields are present. Presence should be tested with key membership or `is not None`, not truthiness.

findings.title: Hook now returns undefined attributes during the initial fetch
findings.body: Previously this hook always constructed and returned a `TagCollection` (an empty object while the request had no data). The replacement returns `previous` while `isFetching`; on the first request both `data` and `previous` are undefined. Existing consumers of `attributes`/`tags` can therefore receive undefined rather than a collection and fail when enumerating or spreading it. Preserve an empty-object fallback while no cached result exists.
